findings.title: operationId is not unique across routes whose urls differ only in separators
findings.detail: operationIdOf collapses every run of non-alphanumerics into a single underscore, so two public routes such as GET /api/v1/a-b and GET /api/v1/a/b both get operationId get_api_v1_a_b. No criterion pins the behaviour for colliding urls and OpenAPI expects unique operationIds.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN two public routes have urls that differ only in non-alphanumeric characters THEN buildOpenApiDocument gives both operations the same operationId.

findings.title: Same-digest call on an expired done key reruns fn instead of replaying
findings.detail: The claim replaces any row whose created_at is at or before the cutoff regardless of digest, so calling again after 24 hours with the same digest runs fn again (replayed false) rather than replaying the stored response. The expiry scenario only pins the different-digest case.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN a done key created 24 hours or more before now is called again with the same digest THEN withIdempotency claims it as in_progress and runs fn again with replayed false.

findings.title: Undefined body behaves differently with and without Idempotency-Key
findings.detail: respondIdempotent's no-key path passes fn's body straight to reply.send, so a body of undefined produces an empty-bodied answer with fn's status, while the same fn under a key makes JSON.stringify return a non-string and rejects with TypeError (500). No scenario covers an undefined body without a key.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN respondIdempotent runs without an Idempotency-Key and fn returns a body of undefined THEN it calls reply.code(result.status).send(undefined) instead of rejecting the way the keyed path does.

findings.title: readPage accepts leading-zero limit strings
findings.detail: No scenario pins down a limit string with leading zeros such as "001" or "01". Two reasonable implementations differ: accept any digit string that parses into 1..200 (what the committed code does) or refuse non-canonical decimal forms. The committed LIMIT_STRING_PATTERN /^[0-9]{1,3}$/ accepts them and Number() parses "001" to 1.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN readPage gets limit "001" THEN it returns { limit: 1, cursor: null }

findings.title: readPage treats a non-object query as empty
findings.detail: No scenario pins down readPage(null) or a non-object query. Two reasonable implementations differ: return the defaults (what the committed asRecord + undefined path does) or throw VALIDATION_FAILED.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN readPage gets a non-object query such as null THEN it returns { limit: 50, cursor: null }
